body.statement:
From a supplied rational interval name \(\mathfrak r\) for \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\), construct a positive rational \(L_J\) and, for every admissible rational interval \(I\subseteq[-G,G]\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), rational endpoints \(\underline J(I,m)\) and \(\overline J(I,m)\), together with finite checkable evaluation witnesses derived from the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas for \(V_0\) and \(V_\gamma\), such that \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) satisfies every enclosure, width, and point-width requirement of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\) for \(J(p,\gamma)\).  In particular, the construction must certify the explicit uniform modulus
\[
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 \leq L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}
\]
and must not take oracle soundness as an input premise.
body.justification: This open target now records exactly the model-specific sound-oracle construction needed for operational certification.
body.gap: Analytic piecewise-Gaussian formulas have not yet been converted into rational enclosures, an explicit certified modulus, and finite checkable evaluation witnesses.
body.consumer: Once discharged, this target will supply the oracle required by the conditional certificate and regret theorems.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(p=(\lambda,\tau,\nu)^{\mathsf T}\), and temporarily write \(\eta\) for the staffing argument of the objective.  We give an explicit construction of the oracle and prove each part of its contract.

First extract rational bounds from one entry of the supplied name \(\mathfrak r\).  The positivity and interior certificates in Definition \(\mathrm{input\mbox{-}name}\), together with Assumptions \(\mathrm{rate\mbox{-}membership}\), \(\mathrm{staffing\mbox{-}cost\mbox{-}positive}\), \(\mathrm{information\mbox{-}cost\mbox{-}positive}\), and \(\mathrm{test\mbox{-}size}\), permit finite rational choices
\[
 0<r_-\leq \lambda,\tau,\nu\leq r_+,
 \quad 0<c_M\leq c_M^+,
 \quad 0<c_I\leq c_I^+,
 \quad 0<\alpha_-\leq\alpha\leq\alpha_+<1,
 \quad 0\leq G\leq g_+.
\]
For example, one may take the minimum of the certified positive lower endpoints and the maximum of the upper endpoints of that entry.  Thus this extraction uses only comparisons of rational numbers.  Put
\[
 d_*=2r_-,\qquad
 q_-={2r_-^2\over 3r_+},\qquad
 q^*={2r_+^2\over 3r_-},\qquad
 v_*={r_-^2\over4r_+^3}.
\]
The definitions of \(d,q,V_0\) give, throughout this rational box,
\[
 d\geq d_*,\qquad q_-\leq q\leq q^*,\qquad
 V_0={2\lambda\tau\over(\lambda+\tau)^3}\geq v_*>0.                                      \tag{1}
\]

We next derive a computable Lipschitz bound in \(\eta\).  Define
\[
 \Psi_\eta(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 {D x^2\over2q},&x\leq\eta,\\[2mm]
 {d x^2\over2q}+{\nu\eta x\over q}-{\nu\eta^2\over2q},&x>\eta,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad w_\eta(x)=\exp\{-\Psi_\eta(x)\},
 \qquad Z_\eta=\int_{\mathbb R}w_\eta(x)\,dx.                                      \tag{2}
\]
The two values and the two first derivatives in \(x\) agree at \(x=\eta\).  Hence (2) has no boundary atom at the moving kink.  Direct differentiation shows
\[
 \Psi_\eta'(x)={d x+\nu\min\{x,\eta\}\over q},
 \qquad
 \partial_\eta\Psi_\eta(x)=s_\eta(x):={\nu\over q}(x-\eta)_+.                    \tag{3}
\]
Consequently the normalized density in (2) is exactly \(\pi_\eta=w_\eta/Z_\eta\) from the frozen definition of \(\pi_\gamma\).  If
\[
 m_\eta={1\over Z_\eta}\int_{\mathbb R}xw_\eta(x)\,dx,
 \qquad
 T_\eta(x)=\int_x^\infty (u-m_\eta)w_\eta(u)\,du,
\]
then the flux formula in Definition \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) yields
\[
 y_\eta(x):=h_\eta'(x)={T_\eta(x)\over q w_\eta(x)},
 \qquad
 V_\eta={2\over qZ_\eta}\int_{\mathbb R}{T_\eta(x)^2\over w_\eta(x)}\,dx.          \tag{4}
\]
This is already a one-dimensional quadrature formula, and all of its inner quantities have explicit Gaussian forms.  To make the later certificate completely concrete, set
\[
 \sigma_L=\sqrt{q/D},\qquad \sigma_R=\sqrt{q/d},\qquad
 \mu_R=-{\nu\eta\over d},\qquad
 C_\eta=\exp\!\left({\nu D\eta^2\over2dq}\right),
\]
and set
\[
 E(t)=e^{-t^2/2},\qquad
 F(t)=\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-u^2/2}\,du=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\Phi(t),
 \qquad \overline F(t)=\sqrt{2\pi}-F(t).
\]
With \(t_L=\eta/\sigma_L\) and \(t_R=(\eta-\mu_R)/\sigma_R\), direct changes of variable and one integration by parts give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z_\eta&=\sigma_LF(t_L)+C_\eta\sigma_R\overline F(t_R),\\
 Z_\eta m_\eta
 &=-\sigma_L^2E(t_L)
   +C_\eta\{\mu_R\sigma_R\overline F(t_R)+\sigma_R^2E(t_R)\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                                       \tag{4a}
\]
Moreover, the centering identity \(\int_{\mathbb R}(u-m_\eta)w_\eta(u)\,du=0\) gives the cancellation-stable flux formulas
\[
 T_\eta(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 \sigma_L^2E(x/\sigma_L)+m_\eta\sigma_LF(x/\sigma_L),&x\leq\eta,\\[1mm]
 C_\eta\bigl[(\mu_R-m_\eta)\sigma_R\overline F((x-\mu_R)/\sigma_R)
       +\sigma_R^2E((x-\mu_R)/\sigma_R)\bigr],&x>\eta.
 \end{cases}                                                                         \tag{4b}
\]
Thus evaluating (4) requires only rational interval evaluations of exponential, square root, \(\Phi\), and one final proper quadrature after a certified tail truncation.
Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives the uniform pointwise bounds
\[
 {1\over D}\leq y_\eta(x)\leq {1\over d}.                                          \tag{5}
\]

Let \(X\) have density \(\pi_\eta\).  From (3), differentiation under the integral in (2) gives
\[
 m_\eta'=-\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_\eta}\{X,s_\eta(X)\}.                            \tag{6}
\]
This differentiation is justified by a quadratic Gaussian envelope: \(\Psi_\eta\) is \(d/q\)-strongly convex, uniformly on each side of the kink, and is continuously differentiable at the kink.  The same envelope justifies all differentiations below.

We record bounds needed in (6).  By reversibility, the Poisson equation and integration by parts give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\eta}(X)
 =\int (x-m_\eta)(-\mathcal L_\eta h_\eta)(x)\pi_\eta(x)\,dx
 =q\int y_\eta(x)\pi_\eta(x)\,dx
 \leq {q\over d},                                                                    \tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality is (5).  For an independent copy \(X'\), the covariance identity and the \(\nu/q\)-Lipschitz property of \(s_\eta\) imply
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Cov}\{X,s_\eta(X)\}\right|
 =\left|{1\over2}\mathbb E[(X-X')\{s_\eta(X)-s_\eta(X')\}]\right|
 \leq {\nu\over q}\operatorname{Var}(X)
 \leq {\nu\over d}.                                                                 \tag{8}
\]

Differentiate the first-order form of the Poisson equation,
\[
 qy_\eta'(x)-\{dx+\nu\min(x,\eta)\}y_\eta(x)=m_\eta-x.
\]
With \(z_\eta=\partial_\eta y_\eta\), equations (5), (6), and (8) give
\[
 qz_\eta'(x)-\{dx+\nu\min(x,\eta)\}z_\eta(x)
 =g_\eta(x):=m_\eta'+\nu\mathbf 1\{x>\eta\}y_\eta(x),
 \qquad \|g_\eta\|_\infty\leq {2\nu\over d}.                                    \tag{9}
\]
The flux integration-by-parts identity \(\operatorname{Cov}\{X,f(X)\}=q\mathbb E[y_\eta(X)f'(X)]\), first for smooth \(f\) and then by Lipschitz approximation, applied to \(f=s_\eta\) combines with (6) to give \(m_\eta'=-\nu\mathbb E[y_\eta(X)\mathbf 1\{X>\eta\}]\).  Hence \(\int g_\eta\pi_\eta=0\).  If \(\mu_\eta\) is the unique minimizer of \(\Psi_\eta\), strong convexity gives, for \(x\leq\mu_\eta\),
\[
 {\int_{-\infty}^x\pi_\eta(u)\,du\over\pi_\eta(x)}
 \leq\int_0^\infty e^{-dt^2/(2q)}\,dt,
\]
and gives the analogous right-tail inequality for \(x\geq\mu_\eta\).  Solving (9) by its integrating factor and using the smaller of these two tails therefore gives
\[
 \|z_\eta\|_\infty
 \leq {2\nu\over d}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2dq}}.                                         \tag{10}
\]
Notice that (9)--(10) also verify the kink case: the coefficient has a jump in its derivative only on a set of stationary measure zero, while (3) vanishes at the joining point, so no unaccounted moving-boundary term occurs.

The minimizer is explicit:
\[
 \mu_\eta=0\quad(\eta\geq0),
 \qquad
 \mu_\eta=-{\nu\eta\over d}\quad(\eta<0).                                          \tag{11}
\]
Integration of the derivative of \((x-\mu_\eta)e^{-\Psi_\eta(x)}\), followed by strong convexity, yields
\[
 1=\mathbb E[(X-\mu_\eta)\Psi_\eta'(X)]
 \geq {d\over q}\mathbb E[(X-\mu_\eta)^2].                                         \tag{12}
\]
It follows from (11)--(12), for \(|\eta|\leq G\), that
\[
 \mathbb E[(X-\eta)_+]
 \leq G\left(1+{\nu\over d}\right)+\sqrt{q/d}.                                    \tag{13}
\]

Since \(\partial_\eta\log\pi_\eta=-s_\eta+\mathbb E s_\eta\), differentiation of the energy in (4) gives the exact identity
\[
 V_\eta'
 =2q\,\mathbb E\left[2y_\eta z_\eta-
       \{s_\eta-\mathbb E s_\eta\}y_\eta^2\right].                               \tag{14}
\]
Using (5), (10), the nonnegativity of \(s_\eta\), and (13) in (14) proves
\[
 |V_\eta'|
 \leq {8\nu q\over d^2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2dq}}
 +{4\nu\over d^2}\left[G\left(1+{\nu\over d}\right)+\sqrt{q/d}\right].          \tag{15}
\]
All bounds remain finite at every asymmetric corner of the original rate box because \(q_->0\) and \(d_*>0\).

We now turn (15) into a rational certificate.  By finite searches over positive rationals choose \(s_1,s_2,s_0\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that
\[
 s_1^2>{2\over d_*q_-},\qquad
 s_2^2>{q^*\over d_*},\qquad
 s_0^2>{1\over v_*}.
\]
The first inequality is valid for the square root in (15) because \(\pi<4\).  Define the rational number
\[
 B_*={8r_+q^*\over d_*^2}s_1
 +{4r_+\over d_*^2}\left[g_+\left(1+{r_+\over d_*}\right)+s_2\right].               \tag{16}
\]
Choose an integer \(z^*>0\) with \((z^*)^2>2/\alpha_-\).  If \(Z\) is standard normal, Chebyshev's inequality, proved here by
\(\Pr(|Z|\geq z)\leq\mathbb E Z^2/z^2=1/z^2\), shows
\(1-\Phi(z^*)<\alpha_-/2\).  Hence \(0<z_\alpha<z^*\).  Equations (1), (15), and (16), followed by the ordinary chain rule, now give
\[
 \left|{\partial\over\partial\eta}J(p,\eta)\right|
 \leq c_M^+ + {c_I^+z^*B_*s_0\over2}.
\]
Thus the following is an explicit positive rational global modulus:
\[
 L_J=1+c_M^+ + {c_I^+z^*B_*s_0\over2}.                                               \tag{17}
\]
In particular, the mean-value theorem and (17) prove
\[
 |J(p,\eta)-J(p,\xi)|\leq L_J|\eta-\xi|,
 \qquad \eta,\xi\in[-G,G].                                                           \tag{18}
\]

For completeness, we next construct a finite, rationally checkable point evaluator; this is the part that turns the analytic formula into an objective oracle rather than assuming an oracle.  Given rational \(\eta\in[-g_+,g_+]\) and \(k\in\mathbb N\), the evaluator \(\mathsf E(\eta,k)=[e^-(\eta,k),e^+(\eta,k)]\) is produced as follows.

Use the two Gaussian pieces in (2), the moment formula and the flux-energy formula (4).  Multiplying \(w_\eta\) by \(e^{\Psi_\eta(\mu_\eta)}\) changes neither \(\pi_\eta\), \(m_\eta\), \(y_\eta\), nor \(V_\eta\).  For this rescaled weight, strong convexity and (11) give
\[
 0<\widetilde w_\eta(x)
 \leq \exp\left\{-{d_*\over2q^*}(x-\mu_\eta)^2\right\},
 \qquad |\mu_\eta|\leq {r_+g_+\over d_*}.                                          \tag{19}
\]
Choose a rational \(R>1+r_+g_+/d_*\).  The elementary integration-by-parts bounds
\[
 \int_a^\infty e^{-\kappa t^2/2}\,dt
 \leq {e^{-\kappa a^2/2}\over\kappa a},
 \qquad
 \int_a^\infty t e^{-\kappa t^2/2}\,dt
 ={e^{-\kappa a^2/2}\over\kappa},                                                    \tag{20}
\]
with \(\kappa=d_*/q^*\), give rationally certifiable tail enclosures for \(Z_\eta\) and its first moment after enclosing the exponential.  They tend to zero as \(R\to\infty\).  Independently, (5), (11), (12), and Markov's inequality give the energy-tail certificate
\[
 2q\,\mathbb E\!left[y_\eta(X)^2\mathbf 1\{|X|>R\}\right]
 \leq {2(q^*)^2\over d_*^3\{R-r_+g_+/d_*\}^2}.                                     \tag{21}
\]
Thus a finite integer search finds \(R\) for which every tail contribution requested by precision \(k\) is below any prescribed rational fraction of \(2^{-k}\).

On \([-R,R]\), split the interval at \(\eta\).  Compute intervals for \(Z_\eta\) and \(m_\eta\) from (4a), compute the flux on every cell from the appropriate branch of (4b), and enclose the final integral in (4) by upper and lower Darboux sums.  Exponentials are enclosed by range-reduced Taylor intervals and the occurrences of \(F\) and \(\overline F\) are enclosed through the certified normal integral (22) below.  Every denominator is certified away from zero: \(q\geq q_-\); either positive term in (4a) gives \(Z_\eta>0\); and continuity and positivity of \(w_\eta\) give a positive rational lower bound on \([-R,R]\).  The input box is refined from \(\mathfrak r\) until these lower bounds are exposed.  Inequality (21) is then added symmetrically to the truncated energy interval, so the result encloses the full integral.

These enclosures are finite and checkable using rational arithmetic.  More explicitly, for \(|u|\leq1\), the first \(n\) terms of the exponential series have a remainder bounded by \(3/(n+1)!\); repeated squaring after replacing an arbitrary bounded argument by \(u/2^j\) supplies a rational exponential interval.  Rational square-root intervals are obtained by bisection and comparison of squares.  The identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\]
follows by the tangent addition formula, and the alternating arctangent series supplies rational upper and lower bounds with the first omitted term as remainder.  Hence the normalizing constant used by \(\Phi\) also has finite rational witnesses.

For \(z_\alpha\), restrict to \([0,z^*]\).  Certified Darboux sums for
\[
 \Phi(z)={1\over2}+{1\over\sqrt{2\pi}}
                    \int_0^z e^{-t^2/2}\,dt                                          \tag{22}
\]
and refinements of the supplied interval for \(\alpha\) yield a certified bracket for the unique solution of \(\Phi(z)=1-\alpha/2\).  Termination is quantitative: on \([0,z^*]\),
\[
 \Phi'(z)\geq {e^{-(z^*)^2/2}\over\sqrt{2\pi}}>0,
\]
and a rational positive lower bound is obtained by the preceding exponential and square-root enclosures.  A rational grid of sufficiently small mesh, retaining exactly the cells whose certified \(\Phi\)-images meet the current interval for \(1-\alpha/2\), therefore has hull width at most the mesh plus the evaluation and input widths divided by that derivative lower bound.  Refining all three quantities gives any requested bracket width.

The preceding procedure terminates for the energy as well.  Indeed, (19)--(21) make the discarded tails arbitrarily small.  On the retained compact interval, each piece of every integrand is continuously differentiable with bounded derivative; the two pieces meet continuously at \(\eta\).  Therefore the difference of its upper and lower Darboux sums is bounded by its certified derivative bound times the mesh length.  The widths caused by the input name tend to zero because all displayed operations are rational operations, exponentials, square roots, and divisions by the positive lower bounds just exhibited.  Refining the input index, Taylor orders, \(R\), and the rational meshes must consequently produce a finite trace satisfying
\[
 J(p,\eta)\in\mathsf E(\eta,k),
 \qquad e^+(\eta,k)-e^-(\eta,k)\leq2^{-k}.                                           \tag{23}
\]
The trace consists of the chosen input index, \(R\), the two rational partitions, Taylor orders and remainder inequalities, denominator lower bounds, the tail inequalities (20)--(21), the quantile grid and (22), and the final interval-arithmetic expression.  A verifier checks only finitely many rational inequalities and integer factorials.  Thus (23) supplies the finite checkable evaluation witnesses demanded in the theorem.

It remains to assemble interval evaluations.  For a rational interval \(I=[a,b]\subseteq[-G,G]\), let
\[
 \eta_I={a+b\over2},\qquad \Delta_I=b-a,
 \qquad [e^-,e^+]=\mathsf E(\eta_I,m),
\]
and define rational endpoints
\[
 \underline J(I,m)=e^- -{L_J\Delta_I\over2},
 \qquad
 \overline J(I,m)=e^+ +{L_J\Delta_I\over2}.                                         \tag{24}
\]
For every \(\eta\in I\), (18), (23), and \(|\eta-\eta_I|\leq\Delta_I/2\) show
\[
 J(p,\eta)\in[\underline J(I,m),\overline J(I,m)].
\]
Moreover, (23)--(24) give the required explicit modulus,
\[
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 \leq L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}.                                               \tag{25}
\]
If \(I\) is a point interval, \(\Delta_I=0\), so its returned width is at most \(2^{-m}\).  Equations (17), (23), and (24), together with their finite rational traces, therefore construct \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) from the supplied input name and verify every enclosure, width, and point-width clause of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\).  Oracle soundness has been derived rather than used as a premise.
